function.name: comment
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Comment on a tweet for the authenticated user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tweet_id.description: ID of the tweet to comment on.

function.name: follow_user
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Follow a user for the authenticated user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

username_to_follow.description: Username of the user to follow.

follow_status.description: True if followed, False if already following.

function.name: get_tweet
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Retrieve a specific tweet. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tweet_id.description: ID of the tweet to retrieve.

tags.description: List of tags associated with the tweet.

mentions.description: List of users mentioned in the tweet.

function.name: get_tweet_comments
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Retrieve all comments for a specific tweet. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tweet_id.description: ID of the tweet to retrieve comments for.

comments.description: List of dictionaries, each containing comment information.

function.name: get_user_stats

username.description: Username of the user to get statistics for.

tweet_count.description: Number of tweets posted by the user.

following_count.description: Number of users the specified user is following.

retweet_count.description: Number of retweets made by the user.

function.name: get_user_tweets

It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Move a file or directory from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

source.description: Source name of the file or directory to move. Source must be local to the current directory.

destination.description: The destination name to move the file or directory to. Destination must be local to the current directory and cannot be a path. If destination is not an existing directory like when renaming something, destination is the new file name.

result.description: The result of the move operation.

function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Return the current working directory path. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Sort the contents of a file line by line. function.name: tail
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Display the last part of a file of any extension. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the file to display. No path is allowed and you can only perform on file at local directory.

lines.description: The number of lines to display from the end of the file. Defaults to 10.

function.name: touch
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Create a new file of any extension in the current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the new file in the current directory. file_name is local to the current directory and does not allow path.

function.name: wc
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Count the number of lines, words, and characters in a file of any extension from current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: Name of the file of current directory to perform wc operation on.

mode.description: Mode of operation ('l' for lines, 'w' for words, 'c' for characters).

count.description: The count of the number of lines, words, or characters in the file.

type.description: The type of unit we are counting. [Enum]: ["lines", "words", "characters"]

function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Write content to a file at current directory or display it in the terminal.

content.description: The content to write or display.

file_name.description: The name of the file at current directory to write the content to. Defaults to None.

terminal_output.description: The content if no file name is provided, or None if written to file.
